friction.step: README.md 'Use the surfaces in your own project' — copy-pasting the ```bash bootstrap block verbatim
friction.detail: The prose right above the code block tells the agent to add `"registry": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/conmeara/ui-backlot/main/registry"` to hyperframes.json, but the runnable ```bash block directly below it skips that edit entirely — it goes straight from `npx hyperframes init my-video ...` to `npx hyperframes add excel-workbook`. I reproduced this literally (fresh init, no manual registry edit, ran the block's exact commands): `hyperframes.json` still had the default `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/main/registry`, and `npx hyperframes add excel-workbook` failed with `Item "excel-workbook" not found in registry`, dumping a long list of unrelated heygen stock items (warm-grain, play-mode, vignelli, us-map, caption-pill-karaoke, ...). A stranger who copies the fenced code block instead of reading the prose carefully hits a hard error on their very first install command.
friction.suggestedFix: In README.md, insert the hyperframes.json registry edit as an explicit step inside the ```bash block itself (e.g. a `jq`/sed one-liner or a comment-annotated manual-edit line) between `npx hyperframes init ...` and the first `npx hyperframes add ...`, so the block is actually copy-paste-safe and matches the prose above it.

friction.detail: The Verify step lists `npm run registry:check`, `npm run hf:lint`, `npm run hf:validate`, `npm run hf:inspect` as 'Before sharing a reusable demo workflow' with no caveat that these are ui-backlot-repo-internal npm scripts (defined in the monorepo's own package.json). None of them exist in a project scaffolded by `npx hyperframes init` — an external consumer's package.json only has `dev`/`check`/`render`/`publish`. Running any of the four listed commands in the consumer project fails with `npm error Missing script`. The doc never states the consumer-side equivalent (`npx hyperframes check .` / the scaffolded `npm run check`).
friction.suggestedFix: In docs/guides/build-hyperframes-demo.md section 5, split the Verify list into 'If you're working in this repo' (the four npm run commands) vs 'If you installed via the registry into your own project' (`npx hyperframes check .` or `npm run check`), so external consumers aren't pointed at commands that don't exist for them.

friction.detail: Installing claude-composed-app silently pulled in four extra composition files documented elsewhere in docs/catalog.md as deprecated: claude-agent-rail.html, claude-composer.html, claude-sidebar.html, claude-thread-core.html. README's 'one surface (foundation CSS + fonts install automatically)' callout only mentions fonts/CSS auto-installing, not extra deprecated composition HTML files landing in compositions/. Harmless (they're internal deps of the composed shell) but nothing in the allowed docs explains why deprecated-tagged files show up in a fresh install, which is disorienting when cross-referencing against docs/catalog.md's deprecation notes.
friction.suggestedFix: Add a line near the README 'one surface (foundation CSS + fonts install automatically)' note clarifying that some blocks also pull in internal sub-part dependencies (even ones separately catalogued as deprecated) and that's expected.
